# The Enter-after-picker e2e arm reddens on an orphaned picker node in CI

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingExample.spec.mjs` › `date: Enter after a picker visit commits and hands focus back to the View` landed with PR #18852 (mine). @neo-opus-ada reported it intermittent in CI on PR #18857 — a ComboBox-only source diff — run 35344690108, attempt 2: after Enter the editor is gone, and `.neo-picker-container` stays at count 1 for the whole 5 s of `toHaveCount(0)`. 15/15 locally on `dev@d2082de483` and on her branch.

## The Problem

The arm asserts more than it is about. It exists to prove that Enter after a picker visit commits and leaves focus on `grid.View`. To read focus only after the dying picker is out of the way, it also asserts `await expect(page.locator(PICKER)).toHaveCount(0)` — and that is the assertion that reddens.

Behind it sits an engine sighting the arm cannot own: the DateField's own Enter re-shows its picker in the tick in which the grid's Enter destroys editor and picker, and on a loaded runner the picker's node can stay in the DOM afterwards. Not reproduced locally — 9/9 clean with the main thread throttled up to 8× (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`), the node always added and removed within 20 ms — so it is recorded as a defect-note, not prescribed here.

## The Architectural Reality

Since #18850 a destroyed floating component takes no focus when its mount lands, so the dying picker cannot move focus whether or not its node is removed: the focus read does not need the node to be gone.

## The Fix

Drop the picker-node assertion from the arm; keep the editor's removal, the focus read and the record read-back.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The arm no longer asserts the picker container's absence, and still fails when the engine guard of #18850 is removed (mutation recorded in the PR).
- [ ] `--repeat-each=20` green locally; the CI e2e job green.

## Out of Scope

The orphaned picker node itself (defect-note, to be promoted once it reproduces) · whether a picker field should open its picker on Enter while it is a grid editor.

## Related

#18838 / PR #18852 · #18850 / PR #18856 · PR #18857 (where it reddened) · #18879 (the same runner-load family, in the menu arms).
